runners_data.name: Byron Hill
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with top-class form but 66 days off and 9 years old may struggle with the sustained pace
runners_data.comment: Consistent this year, without looking ready to win again; third to a stablemate latest.
runners_data.spotlight: Sole hurdles win at Carlisle (2m1f, soft; from 8lb higher) in October 2024; consistent this year, without necessarily looking ready to win again; third to better-fancied stablemate Cosmic Soul at Sedgefield (2m4f, good) nine weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Rickety Gate
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts him in the danger zone when traffic problems develop 2-3 out
runners_data.comment: Weakened into seventh at Cartmel (2m6f; beaten 13l+) 12 days ago; others more convincing.
runners_data.spotlight: Back below last winning mark (Carlisle, 2m4f) but pulled up at Ayr on penultimate start, and weakened into seventh at Cartmel (2m6f; beaten over 13l) 12 days ago; others more convincing at this stage.

runners_data.name: Fine Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to this pace setup, raised 7lb but tackling 2m4f for first time
runners_data.comment: Resumed winning ways over 2m here (good) latest; 7lb higher; Patrick Mullins is booked.
runners_data.spotlight: Steady progress since joining this trainer, resuming winning ways over 2m here (good; 7-2, with Malangen third) latest; raised 7lb since, and tackles 2m4f for the first time; noteworthy that Patrick Mullins travels over from Ireland to ride.

runners_data.name: Malangen
runners_data.note: Sole leader will get easy time early but 11-year-old stamina questionable when pressured late
runners_data.comment: Staying-on third to Fine Point here (2m, good; 100-30 fav) latest; return to 2m4f helpful.
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 2m here (good; from 13lb higher) in June 2024; seems to be gradually working back to form, a staying-on third to Fine Point here (2m, good; 100-30 favourite) latest; hopes of reversal over 2m4f on 7lb better terms.

runners_data.name: Ushuaia Dancer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 67-day break but avoids early trouble and has course experience
runners_data.comment: Returning from a lengthy absence when runner-up at Newcastle (2m4f; 18-1) in March.
runners_data.spotlight: Only win came courtesy of the stewards' at Newcastle (2m6f, heavy) in January 2024; was returning from a lengthy absence when runner-up to a Skelton-runner at Newcastle (2m4f; 18-1) in March; realistic prospect of easing conditions would aid his cause.

runners_data.name: My My My Delilah
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but 12-race maiden status suggests class limitations will show
runners_data.comment: 12-race maiden; weakened quickly at Kelso (2m, good; sixth, btn 21l) latest; easing mark.
runners_data.spotlight: 12-race maiden; pulled up over 2m here (soft) on penultimate start, and weakened quickly at Kelso (2m, good; sixth, beaten 21l) subsequently; continues to ease in the weights, now 17lb lower than back in January.

runners_data.name: Cuillin Ridge
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who changed stables for £12,500, headgear removed suggests confidence
runners_data.comment: Ridden out to score at Huntingdon (3m1f; from 6lb lower) in March; since sold for £12,500.
runners_data.spotlight: Ridden out to score at Huntingdon (3m1f, novices' handicap; good to soft; from 6lb lower) in March; has since left Henry Daly for £12,500; headgear removed, and interesting to see what the market makes of his chance off a three-month break; merits respect.

runners_data.name: Road To Rosley
runners_data.note: Prominent style into traffic problems, winless record and beaten 50 lengths last time
runners_data.comment: Yet to win (0-12) and beaten almost 50l in a Cartmel maiden (2m6f; 100-1) a fortnight ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to win (0-12) and beaten almost 50l in a Cartmel maiden (2m6f; 100-1) a fortnight ago; no reason to expect better for this return to handicapping; the first one to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Follow The Leader
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but 496 days since last rules run despite point form, unknown quantity
runners_data.comment: Productive in points (form 212) this spring, runner-up at Witton Castle (3m) last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in three maiden hurdles (massive prices) in late 2024/early 2025; productive in points (form 212) this spring, chasing home Getupearly at Witton Castle (3m) last month; tough to know what to expect but isn't totally dismissed.

runners_data.name: C'Mon So
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but beaten by huge margins in recent hurdle starts, needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Five-race rules maiden; beaten 50l, 54l, and 36l, in three hurdle starts; handicap debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in a point; five-race rules maiden; beaten 50l, 54l, and 36l, in three hurdle starts (2m-2m4f maiden/novices'); significant improvement is needed to make an impression on this handicap debut.

races.paceDynamic: Malangen will be the sole early leader with Byron Hill, Rickety Gate, Cuillin Ridge and C'Mon So all wanting prominent positions behind him. This creates significant congestion in the prominent pack, with Malangen likely to get an uncontested lead through the early stages before the prominent quartet begin to jostle for position approaching the business end. The step up to 2m4f and good going should create a sustained gallop that will test stamina reserves, particularly when the prominent runners start to pressure Malangen from 3 out. This pace setup and distance strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early traffic and have the class to finish strongly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack gets into a scrap for position from 3 out while pressuring Malangen.
scenarios.body: The early pace battle will set up perfectly for the back markers to sweep through with late challenges. Fine Point and Ushuaia Dancer have the class advantage and tactical positioning to capitalise when others have emptied their tanks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Survive
scenarios.trigger: If Malangen gets too easy a lead and one prominent horse detaches cleanly.
scenarios.body: Byron Hill or Cuillin Ridge could steal a march on the field if they can avoid the traffic problems and kick clear before the hold-up horses get organised. Malangen's stamina reserves might just see him through if not pressured early enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Malangen goes too fast early trying to shake off the prominent pack.
scenarios.body: The entire field could come back to the leaders in the final half-mile, creating a messy sprint finish where any horse with a clear run could prevail. This chaotic finish might suit an unconsidered runner breaking through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Class Order Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the race runs to form despite tactical complications.
scenarios.body: The highest-rated horses simply outclass their rivals regardless of how the race unfolds. Byron Hill and Fine Point use their superior ratings to overcome any positional disadvantages.

watchPoints.text: Rickety Gate and Byron Hill could get squeezed out when the prominent pack converges 2-3 out
Malangen may get too easy a lead early before being swamped by classier finishers in the straight
Fine Point stepping up to 2m4f for first time after winning over 2m here 18 days ago
Follow The Leader returning to rules after 496 days off despite recent point wins
Cuillin Ridge headgear removal after stable change suggests connections expect improved performance

races.name: Most Important 3-Year-Old Race Today Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sudbury Hill
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with best flat form who should handle the lead role without early pressure, 23 days since last run is ideal
runners_data.comment: Fairly useful on Flat; trainer/jockey supplied the wide-margin winner of this last year.
runners_data.spotlight: Productive on the Flat (best RPR 82), with plenty to admire about the manner in which he applied himself going down to King Of Berkshire at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm) on penultimate start; trainer/jockey supplied the wide-margin winner of this (One Horse Town) last year; looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Tiny Riot
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from powerful Dan Skelton yard, 59 days off the flat may need this run but stable in excellent form
runners_data.comment: Fifth of nine on Flat handicap debut at Nottingham (1m2f, good; 14-1) in April; possible.
runners_data.spotlight: Made progress - at his own rate - on the Flat, seeming to handle the extra yardage when fifth of nine on handicap debut at Nottingham (1m2f, good; 14-1) in April; bit to find with Sudbury Hill on Flat figures, but it would be foolhardy to dismiss a Skelton-trained jumps newcomer.

runners_data.name: Mount Eden
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with fading tendency, half-brothers successful over hurdles suggests stamina but flat form uninspiring
runners_data.comment: Modest on the Flat for D. O'Brien (0-4); half-brother to two hurdle winners; Irish raider.
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't offer much on the Flat for Donnacha O'Brien (0-4) prior to changing hands; his half-brothers Waver and Gold Seal were both successful over hurdles (2m); a first ever Hexham runner for the County Wexford handler Shay Slevin.

runners_data.name: Cracking Anna
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with concerning fading pattern, gets 7lb weight allowance but beaten 8+ lengths in low-grade flat race
runners_data.comment: Flat form for Michael Bell isn't overly encouraging; dam won over hurdles though (2m5f)
runners_data.spotlight: Flat form for Michael Bell isn't overly encouraging, beaten in excess of 8l in a 1m2f Class 6 at Yarmouth (good; 12-1) six weeks ago; dam won over hurdles though (2m5f) and she's in pretty safe hands with Greenall and Guerriero; receives the 7lb fillies' allowance.

runners_data.name: Jambearee
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with fading issues, added cheekpieces suggest connections trying to sharpen him up, Brian Ellison has poor recent record
runners_data.comment: Lowly rated on Flat (0-6); trainers representative in this in 2024 was an early casualty.
runners_data.spotlight: Lowly rated on the Flat (0-6); never better than midfield in added cheekpieces at Thirsk (1m4f, Class 5; beaten over 10l, 40-1) three weeks ago; trainers sole representative in this in 2024 was an early casualty; stablemate of Steel Fixer.

runners_data.name: Steel Fixer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who is the marginally better-rated of the Brian Ellison pair, Nathan Moscrop's booking suggests stable confidence
runners_data.comment: Flat maiden (0-6); raced freely and weakened on AW at Newcastle (1m2f) on Tuesday evening.
runners_data.spotlight: Flat maiden (0-6) but marginally higher-rated than stablemate Jambearee, and the fact that Nathan Moscrop takes the ride suggests he's their principal hope; raced too freely and weakened on AW at Newcastle (1m2f) on Tuesday; wears first-time cheekpieces.

races.paceDynamic: Sudbury Hill will likely set a moderate pace from the front with no obvious challengers for the early lead, given most runners prefer to race prominently or be held up. Jambearee may try to track the leader early but has shown a tendency to fade, while the majority of the field (Tiny Riot, Mount Eden, Cracking Anna, Steel Fixer) will settle towards the rear. This sets up a race where the early leader can dictate terms without pressure, creating a tactical advantage for horses that can travel well in behind and have a finishing kick. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay on late when the pace inevitably quickens from the final hurdle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Sudbury Hill sets an even gallop without early pressure from Jambearee
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows the hold-up brigade to close from off the speed when the race develops. Tiny Riot and Steel Fixer can use their stamina reserves in the final half-furlong having conserved energy early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Escapes
scenarios.trigger: If Sudbury Hill's class on the flat translates to jumping and he gets an easy lead
scenarios.body: His proven ability gives him the tactical edge to kick clear after the last when the field is still struggling to get into the race. The hold-up horses find themselves with too much ground to make up despite their preferred running style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both Sudbury Hill and Jambearee fail to maintain a reasonable gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the final flight where stamina counts for nothing and raw speed dominates. This neutralizes the staying advantages of the hold-up horses and creates chaos in the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Pace Duel
scenarios.trigger: If Jambearee decides to challenge Sudbury Hill for the early lead despite his fading tendencies
scenarios.body: Both pace-setters compromise each other's chances by going too fast early, setting up the race perfectly for closers. The backmarkers get the ideal scenario with a strong pace to aim at.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Jambearee tries to make it a pace duel with Sudbury Hill early as both could compromise their chances
Watch for market support for Steel Fixer given Nathan Moscrop's booking suggests he's preferred over stablemate Jambearee
Watch how Tiny Riot travels through the race after 59 days off as Dan Skelton runners often need their first run back

runners_data.name: Dream Jet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with dual course wins sits 5lb below last winning mark, solid claims if pace develops
runners_data.comment: Dual course winner (2m); remote third to Conquer The Breeze here latest; focus elsewhere.
runners_data.spotlight: Dual course winner (2m), who sits 5lb below his last winning mark; finished a remote third to Conquer The Breeze here latest, so it's difficult to work out how he goes about making up such a deficit, even acknowledging more favourable terms.

runners_data.note: Late-running type who won well at course and distance 18 days ago, 5lb rise appears fair

runners_data.spotlight: Saw it out well to get off the mark over fences (C&D), beating Out On Her Own by 7l 18 days ago; a 5lb rise looks fair - competitive off similar marks over hurdles - so he'll be a live contender.

runners_data.name: Halpha Soleil

runners_data.spotlight: Yet to win over fences (0-13); third at Doncaster (3m, soft; on first start since wind surgery) in February, but well beaten at Sedgefield a fortnight later; absent since (107 days) and now 5lb lower in the handicap; others far safer.

runners_data.name: Similar Story
runners_data.note: Front-rank racer now 12lb lower than last win but poor 2024 form figures offer little encouragement

runners_data.name: Cosmic Blizzard
runners_data.note: Prominent type without a rules win in 18 starts, previous bleeding issues raise reliability concerns
runners_data.comment: Just failed at Kelso (3m, good; beaten neck) last October; had issues since; best watched.
runners_data.spotlight: 0-18 under rules; just failed at Kelso (3m, good; beaten a neck) last October, but has had issues since, twice pulling up at Newcastle (bled from the nose on both occasions), and beaten 83l at Perth (3m) over three weeks ago; best watched.

runners_data.name: Manhattan Valley

runners_data.comment: No impact on rules chase debut at Ffos Las (2m4f, good to soft; 16-1) in April; 3lb lower.
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner (May 2024); little impact over hurdles (0-4) and it was a similar story on chase debut at Ffos Las (2m4f, good to soft; 16-1) in April; now 3lb lower, with Jack Tudor taking over in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Out On Her Own
runners_data.note: Back-marker with consistent hurdles form making second chase start at familiar venue
runners_data.comment: Succumbed to the stronger finish of Passengerontheship over C&D latest; now 5lb better off
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden under rules (0-10), but she posted a series of consistent efforts over hurdles; tried to make all in an added hood over C&D (chase debut) latest, succumbing to the stronger finish of Passengerontheship; is 5lb better off with 7l too find; the task isn't impossible.

races.paceDynamic: The Clonmel Kid will likely set the early pace with Dream Jet and Halpha Soleil tracking close behind, creating a genuine galloping tempo rather than a crawl. Conquer The Breeze and Passengerontheship will sit further back, relying on their hold-up tactics to strike late. The sustained pace over this demanding 2m4f trip at Hexham will stretch the field, particularly testing the prominent racers who may find themselves under pressure approaching the final circuit. This pace scenario clearly favours the hold-up horses who can stay out of trouble early and unleash their finishing kick when others are beginning to tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuine and sustained by The Clonmel Kid and Dream Jet
scenarios.body: The prominent runners will come under pressure turning for home, allowing the back-markers to pick them off with superior finishing kicks. Conquer The Breeze and Passengerontheship are perfectly positioned to exploit this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too strong and burns out the leader
scenarios.body: Dream Jet can use his dual course-winning experience to time his challenge perfectly, sitting just off the pace before striking. His proven ability at this track gives him the edge when others falter from their exertions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Leader
scenarios.trigger: If The Clonmel Kid gets an easy lead and dictates throughout
scenarios.body: His stamina will prove decisive as he can quicken when others are still reorganizing their challenges. The front-runner can exploit any hesitation from the field to steal a decisive advantage approaching the final fence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the principals cancel each other out through tactical battles
scenarios.body: Out On Her Own can use her consistent hurdles form to outrun her maiden status, timing her run perfectly. Her recent chase experience at this course gives her the tactical knowledge to exploit any pace collapse.

runners_data.name: Giovanni Change

runners_data.spotlight: Admirable Market Rasen specialist (six wins there); won over 3m at Wetherby (good; from 2lb lower) in March, but hasn't been at his best since; uncharacteristically laboured (never travelling) when remote third latest; bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Lakefield Flyer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with cheekpieces fitted, recent Plumpton run should have sharpened him but modest level of form
runners_data.comment: Plugged on to finish a modest second at Plumpton (2m1f, good; beaten 21l) 11 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins have come at Downpatrick (2m3f); plugged on to finish a modest second at Plumpton (2m1f, good; beaten 21l) 11 days ago; that should have given him confidence though - fell at Killarney prior - and this extra yardage could suit.

runners_data.name: Foxinthebox
runners_data.note: Prominent racer moving from points to handicap company, blinkers fitted and progressive profile appeals

runners_data.name: No Regrets
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter who won this race in 2023, excellent recent course victory suggests he's back to his best at 12

runners_data.spotlight: Stayed on to win this off topweight back in 2023, and gamely back in the winners' enclosure over C&D (from 5lb lower) latest; his jumping was immaculate that day, with his trainer stating that he had drawn benefit from being able to dominate; this rates as a tougher test.

runners_data.name: Sir Carnegie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form with two runs in 24 hours at Perth showing his fitness, blinkers retained

runners_data.name: Lights Are Green
runners_data.note: Prominent racer carrying bottom weight, long absence but third here recently suggests return to form
runners_data.comment: Third to in-form Halfway House Lad at Cartmel (3m1f) a fortnight ago; worthy of inspection
runners_data.spotlight: Won off this mark (beat No Regrets by a neck) over C&D in May 2023; struggled last year, often pulling up, but gave an indication he's back in better shape when third to the in-form Halfway House Lad at Cartmel (3m1f, good; 20-1) a fortnight ago; worthy of inspection.

runners_data.name: West Lawn
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who just broke his maiden over course and distance, effectively 6lb well-in after recent victory
runners_data.comment: Off the mark over fences at 20th attempt over C&D (good; 10-1) 18 days ago; 10lb wrong

runners_data.name: Tell Me Again
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making stable debut for Micky Hammond, previous pointing form modest and needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Toiled behind Passengerontheship (btn 78l) over 2m4f here 18 days ago; tough to consider.
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in a 3m point at Loughanmore for Tom Dreaper last October; badly hampered and unseated rider on stable debut, but left toiling behind Passengerontheship (beaten 78l) over 2m4f here 18 days ago; tough to consider on that evidence.

races.paceDynamic: No Regrets will take the field along at a sustainable gallop from the front, with Giovanni Change, Foxinthebox and Lights Are Green content to track closely behind. The lack of genuine pace pressure means the leaders won't be softened up, allowing them to maintain their positions deep into the race. With only one confirmed front-runner and several prominent racers happy to sit handy, this sets up perfectly for those who can stay close to the pace throughout. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with tactical pace who can avoid getting caught wide or too far back in the testing Hexham finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If No Regrets dictates terms unchallenged and the pace stays even throughout
scenarios.body: The leaders maintain their advantage as the pace doesn't collapse, making it difficult for hold-up horses to make significant ground. Those positioned prominently can kick clear in the straight without having been softened up by early pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Acceleration Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly from the second-last fence as multiple horses challenge
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop sets up a proper staying test where only the fittest horses can respond to the final acceleration. This favours horses with proven stamina who have been conserving energy in mid-division.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Rank Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If No Regrets weakens dramatically and the prominent horses fail to capitalize
scenarios.body: The early leaders fade badly in the final half-mile, opening the door for hold-up horses to sweep through. Patient tactics prove decisive as the pace judgement of those tracking becomes critical.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Misfire
scenarios.trigger: If Giovanni Change or Foxinthebox get trapped behind a weakening No Regrets
scenarios.body: The race becomes messy as the main pace-makers bunch up and hinder each other's progress. This creates opportunities for horses coming from different angles or those who can find clear room.

watchPoints.text: No Regrets must be monitored for signs of stopping as his front-running tactics could backfire if he goes too hard early
Giovanni Change may struggle if his recent form decline continues and he cannot match the pace of more progressive rivals
Sir Carnegie's fitness after two runs in 24 hours at Perth could be either a positive or negative depending on recovery
Foxinthebox is stepping up significantly in class from point-to-pointing and may find this level too sharp
Always Busy needs patient tactics from Jack Tudor to be produced with one decisive run in the closing stages

runners_data.name: Mojito Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Non-runner - prominent style would have suited the likely pace scenario perfectly
runners_data.comment: Fast-closing second to King Al at Ascot (2m; 25-1) in March; Cobden travels to ride.
runners_data.spotlight: French winner for Francois Nicolle; underwent wind surgery after finishing fourth at Newbury in February, and posted a career best when a fast-closing second to King Al at Ascot (2m, good; 25-1) in March; 4lb higher, with Harry Cobden travelling for this sole ride.

runners_data.name: Pyramid Place
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 105 days with recent bleeding issues, needs everything to fall right from the back
runners_data.comment: Pulled up over fences (bled from nose) on final start for Harriet Dickin; best watched.
runners_data.spotlight: 9-39 hurdles, but no win since quickening clear in a four-runner Class 2 at Kempton (2m5f, good; from 19lb higher) in November 2024; pulled up over fences (bled from nose) on final start for Harriet Dickin nearly four months ago; best watched on stable debut (£6,000 purchase).

runners_data.name: Glory And Honour
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who excels at this track with recent course form, well-suited to track the lone leader
runners_data.comment: Low key over fences at Kelso recently, and also has a fair bit to prove back over hurdles.
runners_data.spotlight: Won over fences here (2m, good; in first-time blinkers - two finished) last June; runner-up at Newcastle (2m4f) in April, but low key at Kelso subsequently; returns to hurdles for the first time since finishing tailed off over C&D last October; others more appealing.

runners_data.name: Freddy Robinson
runners_data.note: Prominent style fits the race shape but returning after 184 days, though showed resolution in last hurdles win
runners_data.comment: Won on last spin over hurdles; runner-up on the Flat at Beverley (1m4f) just ten days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Dug in to score on his last spin over hurdles at Market Rasen (2m, good to soft; from 3lb lower) in December; runner-up three times in succession on the Flat at Beverley recently, beaten 2l there (1m4f; 13-8 favourite) just ten days ago.

runners_data.name: Two Auld Pals
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying 9lb penalty for recent course win, claimed rider reduces weight but tactical disadvantage remains
runners_data.comment: Bounded clear over C&D (a 23l winner) four weeks ago; 9lb higher, and up in grade; player.
runners_data.spotlight: Handled testing conditions best, bounding clear to make it 2-3 over C&D (soft; a 23l winner) four weeks ago; the handicapper has reacted, and he's now 9lb higher moving up into a Class 4; still enters calculations though, with 10lb claimer Gregor Walkingshaw retaining the ride.

runners_data.name: Stay In The Game
runners_data.note: Lone leader with 5lb claimer, recent breakthrough win gives confidence but small fields can expose front runners
runners_data.comment: Downed long-odds-on favourite in a match at Huntingdon (2m) 12 days ago; this is tougher.
runners_data.spotlight: Made the breakthrough over hurdles at the seventh attempt, getting the better of the long-odds-on favourite in a match at Huntingdon (2m, good to firm; 6-1) 12 days ago; what that form amounts to is questionable, and this Class 4 contest is much more competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Stay In The Game is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start in this small field of seven. With prominent runners like Mojito Des Mottes, Glory And Honour, and Freddy Robinson likely to track him early, the pace should be honest but sustainable rather than cut-throat. The majority of the field are hold-up horses (Well Educated, Pyramid Place, Two Auld Pals) who will need the pace to develop. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can track the leader and kick when the hold-up horses are still making ground from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Stay In The Game sets a steady tempo and the prominent trackers get first run
scenarios.body: The honest pace allows Glory And Honour, Freddy Robinson, and Mojito Des Mottes to position perfectly and strike before the hold-up brigade can respond. The front division pulls clear as the hold-up horses find too much to do in the small field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too strong or the prominent runners go too early
scenarios.body: Well Educated or Two Auld Pals benefit from a truly-run race where the early pace collapses. Their superior finishing kicks prove decisive as the front-runners tire in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Wire-to-wire Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Stay In The Game gets an easy lead and the field fails to apply pressure
scenarios.body: The 5-year-old exploits the lack of early pace pressure to build an unassailable advantage. His recent Huntingdon win shows he can sustain a gallop when allowed to dictate completely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If no horse commits to tracking Stay In The Game closely through the middle stages
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint where any horse with a turn of foot can capitalize. The lack of early positioning creates chaos in the straight with any style able to prevail.

watchPoints.text: Stay In The Game must be tracked closely early or he could steal a march on this field like at Huntingdon
Well Educated and Two Auld Pals need the prominent runners to go hard early to bring their finishing kicks into play
Freddy Robinson's 184-day absence could tell in the closing stages despite his proven finishing ability
Glory And Honour's track record and tactical position make him the key danger to the pace scenario
The small field size reduces the likelihood of a truly-run race that would suit the hold-up horses

races.name: Tricia Hughes Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Dinons
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 177 days off, cheekpieces applied, veteran needs the uncontested lead to be effective at this trip
runners_data.comment: Hampered and unseated rider when last seen at Newcastle six months ago; advancing years.
runners_data.spotlight: Very useful at his peak, and his last win came from a mark 13lb higher than today's at Uttoxeter (3m, good) in July 2024; hampered and unseated rider when last seen at Newcastle six months ago; difficult to assess how much ability remains at the age of 13.

runners_data.name: Sunset Hill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran well behind Perseus Way here last time, needs strong pace to unleash finishing kick from rear
runners_data.comment: Third to Banderas over 2m4f here (same mark) latest; step back up in trip is the risk.
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up to Thursday's Hamilton scorer Perseus Way over 2m4f here (soft) on penultimate start, and bettered that on RPR's when third to Banderas subsequently; reliable but this step back up to 2m7f mightn't work in her favour; stable won this last year with Pinot Rouge.

runners_data.name: Jeteye
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form with course win 18 days ago, headgear applied but struggles from triple-figure marks historically
runners_data.comment: Rediscovered a spark, scrambling home over C&D (good; 12-1) 18 days ago; now 4lb higher.
runners_data.spotlight: Rediscovered a spark, scrambling home over C&D (good; 12-1) 18 days ago; a 4lb rise takes him back to a triple-figure mark (traditionally struggles from that position) but he isn't one to write off, with this track tending to bring out the best in him.

runners_data.name: Abbey Scope
runners_data.note: Prominent type moving up in trip after Kelso win 31 days ago, strong finish last time suggests this distance will suit
runners_data.comment: Hit the line strongly at Kelso (2m5f; form franked since); up in trip from 6lb higher.
runners_data.spotlight: Added to debut bumper win, hitting the line strongly to score at the third attempt in a handicap hurdle at Kelso (2m5f, good) 31 days ago; moves up in trip (ideal on pedigree) from a 6lb higher mark, with that form franked at Southwell by the third-placed Larkfield Lusive.

runners_data.name: Stylish Recruit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course form carrying lowest weight, headgear applied but disappointing effort at Kelso last time
runners_data.comment: Dual course winner (2m-2m4f); less competitive at Kelso (2m5f; fifth) a fortnight ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Game winner here (2m4f; from 2lb lower) in April; excuse next time (saddle slipped) but less competitive at Kelso (2m5f, good; fifth, beaten 10l) a fortnight ago; needs to bounce back against rivals with a fair amount of upside.

runners_data.name: Robert d'Ores
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three course wins but struggling for form in 2024, headgear applied and needs everything to fall right
runners_data.comment: Three C&D wins; struggling for form in 2026 and has undergone further wind surgery.
runners_data.spotlight: Three C&D wins, the most recent when keeping on well to repel Lelantos (from 2lb higher) last October; struggling for form in 2026 and has undergone further wind surgery since his last appearance five weeks ago; isn't the likeliest.

runners_data.name: Ebselysees
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form for new yard with back-to-back Perth wins, 7lb rise makes task harder despite recent success
runners_data.comment: Won back-to-back at Perth (3m/3m2f); raised further 7lb since latest win; contender.
runners_data.spotlight: Back in the groove since joining the doubly represented Susan Corbett, winning back-to-back at Perth (3m/3m2f); raised a further 7lb since latest win, but that is effectively offset by the returning Rebekah Duffy; worthy of serious consideration in hat-trick mission.

races.paceDynamic: Dinons looks the only confirmed front runner in this small field, likely to dictate terms from the start with Jeteye, Abbey Scope, Stylish Recruit and Ebselysees all prominent runners who will sit just behind. This creates a moderate pace scenario over the extended trip, with Sunset Hill and Robert d'Ores the only hold-up horses forced to come from behind. The lack of genuine pace pressure on Dinons combined with the stamina test of 2m7½f means prominent runners who can track the leader and stay on strongly will have the tactical advantage over pure hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to be effective.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Dinons sets uncontested fractions and prominent runners get first run
scenarios.body: The pace-setters get away with it as hold-up horses struggle to make up ground in time over this staying trip. Abbey Scope and Jeteye benefit most from being close to the pace throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge From Behind
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too hard trying to pressure Dinons mid-race
scenarios.body: The pace collapses in the final half-mile allowing Sunset Hill and Robert d'Ores to sweep past tired leaders. Hold-up horses finally get the strong gallop they need to be effective.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Dinons Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the veteran gets an armchair ride and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: His class advantage tells when getting soft fractions, with the 13-year-old proving his Uttoxeter win was no fluke. The pursuing prominent runners can't match his finishing kick despite the weight concession.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stylish Recruit Course Specialist
scenarios.trigger: If the track knowledge and low weight combination proves decisive
scenarios.body: His previous course win and significant weight advantage allows him to outfinish better-handicapped rivals. The 146lbs burden becomes a major asset in the closing stages.

watchPoints.text: Abbey Scope if taking keen hold early - his strong finish at Kelso suggests he wants this trip but could empty if fighting for position
Dinons for jumping fluency after 177 days off - any mistake could hand initiative to prominent runners tracking behind
Sunset Hill's position turning in - if too far back on this track the hill finish may not provide enough time to get there
Robert d'Ores for signs of returning confidence - three course wins suggest ability is there if headgear helps his focus
Jeteye's weight-carrying ability now back in triple figures - historically struggles when handicapper catches up with him
